in Łódż mammography is performed in a manner that is not consistent with the recommendations.
the doses in the mammography examinations are too high and the quality of the pictures is not good enough.
the doses received by patients in mammography vary greatly, and in a significant part of cases they exceed the values that can be considered safe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of mammography in the context of the dose received by the patient and the quality of diagnostic images.
the problem of the dose received by mammography patients, but it also points to the problem of the quality of the picture and the need for its improvement.
the need of introducing a quality assurance system in the mammography.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mammography is an important diagnostic method in the fight against cancer, but it is also an expensive method, and therefore it should be used only when the quality of picture obtained is satisfactory and the dose received is as low as possible.
the quality of mammography in Poland, as well as in Łódz, is not satisfactory.
the mammographic examination is a very good radiodiagnostic method, provided that it is performed properly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present mammographic practice in Poland is not satisfactory and that it should be improved.
mammography should be performed only in well-equipped and well-qualified radiological laboratories.
mammography is an excellent diagnostic technique but its application should be accompanied by a constant effort of improvement of the quality and a continuous monitoring of doses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mammographic equipment used in the Żeromski Hospital in Łódż, which was the only one that passed all quality control tests, was found to provide a dose level of 4.2 mGy, which is the lowest value among all the mammographs tested.
mammography should be performed in accordance with the rules of good practice, and the mammographs should be serviced regularly and properly maintained.
the quality control should be performed not only in accredited phantom, but also in real clinical conditions, with the use of thermoluminescent dosemeters.
